A '''perfect ruler''' of length <math>\ell</math> is a [[ruler]] with [[integer]] markings <math>a_1=0 < a_2 < \dots < a_n=\ell</math>, for which there exists an integer <math>m</math> such that any [[positive integer]] <math>k\leq m</math> is uniquely expressed as the [[Difference (mathematics)|difference]] <math>k=a_i-a_j</math> for some <math>i,j</math>. This is referred to as an <math>m</math>-perfect ruler.

An [[Optimization (mathematics)|optimal]] perfect ruler is one of the shortest length for fixed values of <math>m</math> and <math>n</math>.

== Example ==

A 4-perfect ruler of length <math>7</math> is given by <math>(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)=(0,1,3,7)</math>. To verify this, we need to show that every positive integer <math>k\leq 4</math> is uniquely expressed as the difference of two markings:
: <math> 1=1-0</math>
: <math> 2=3-1</math>
: <math> 3=3-0</math>
: <math> 4=7-3</math>
